w_heat_cold_drinks.b: A hot week sends people outside and into places where they can sit and cool down.

w_heat_cooling_bill.b: Fridges and air conditioning run flat out in the heat. The power bill for the week is higher than usual.

w_heat_slow_site.t: Crews slow down in the heat at {n}
w_heat_slow_site.b: Work on hot days has to stop early to keep people safe. Output dips for a week.

w_heat_empty_shops.t: Hot weather keeps shoppers away from {n}
w_heat_empty_shops.b: People stay home or head for the beach. Footfall in the shops drops for a few days.

w_cold_heating.t: A cold snap raises heating costs at {n}
w_cold_heating.b: Temperatures fall well below normal and the heating runs day and night.

w_cold_pipes.b: A pipe has frozen and split in the cold. Water is leaking into the back of the premises.

opts.d: An emergency callout. It is fixed within hours.

opts.l: Patch it and wait for the thaw
opts.d: Cheaper today, but the leak may spread.

w_snow_slow.b: Roads are icy and drivers cannot keep to their schedules.

w_snow_quiet.b: Few people go out when the pavements are covered. Takings drop for a few days.

w_snow_hardware.t: Snow shovels and salt fly off the shelves at {n}
w_snow_hardware.b: The first proper snow sends everyone looking for shovels, salt and winter tyres.

w_snow_ski.b: A good fall of snow brings skiers in from the whole region.

w_rain_online.t: Rainy week lifts online orders at {n}
w_rain_online.b: Nobody wants to go out in this weather, so more people shop from the sofa.

w_rain_indoor.b: Families look for something to do under a roof and walk in out of the wet.

w_rain_leak.b: After days of rain water is coming through the ceiling. Part of the premises cannot be used.

opts.d: Costs more now, and it is done for good.
Cheap, but it may fail in the next storm.

w_rain_site.b: Wet ground and standing water stop work on site for several days.

w_storm_deliveries.b: Ferries, roads and flights are disrupted. Goods arrive late and routes have to be changed.

w_storm_sign.b: Wind has torn down a sign and broken some outdoor furniture.

w_storm_power.t: The storm cuts the power to {n}
w_storm_power.b: The grid is down for part of a day. Chilled stock and orders are at risk.

w_sun_terrace.t: Sunny weekend fills the tables at {n}
w_sun_terrace.b: Fine weather brings people out for a long lunch and a drink in the sun.

w_sun_outdoor_work.t: A dry spell speeds up the work at {n}
w_sun_outdoor_work.b: Weeks of dry weather let the crews work long days without interruption.

w_sun_gym_quiet.t: Good weather empties the gym at {n}
w_sun_gym_quiet.b: Members prefer to run and cycle outdoors while the sun is out.

w_heat_farm.b: Weeks of high temperatures are drying out the fields.

opts.d: Extra water and labour keep the yield up.
No extra spend. How much you lose depends on your kit.

w_frost_farm.b: A hard frost after the buds have opened puts this year's harvest at risk.

opts.l: Light fires and run fans overnight
opts.d: Costs labour and fuel, and saves most of the crop.
No effort. The frost may spare more than you fear.

w_xmas_rush.b: Gifts, parties and family dinners bring a few of the busiest weeks of the year.

w_january_slump.b: After the holidays people save money and stay home. The first weeks of the year are slow.

w_gym_resolutions.b: January brings a wave of people who have promised themselves to get fit.

w_summer_quiet_office.t: Summer holidays slow business clients of {n}
w_summer_quiet_office.b: Decision makers are away and projects wait for September.

w_school_return.t: Back to school brings customers to {n}
w_school_return.b: Parents are buying and booking before the new term starts.

w_valentines.b: Couples are booking tables, rooms and gifts.

w_wedding_season.t: Wedding season is under way for {n}
w_wedding_season.b: Couples are booking venues, photographers and planners for the summer.

w_tax_deadline.t: The filing deadline brings a rush to {n}
w_tax_deadline.b: Individuals and companies are looking for help before the tax deadline.

w_black_friday.b: Competitors are cutting prices for the weekend. You can join in, or hold your prices.

opts.d: Some bargain hunters go elsewhere, and your margin holds.
Discounts up front. Busy, but the extra sales may not cover the lost margin.

w_easter_travel.b: A long weekend and school holidays send more people on the road.

w_festival_season.t: A summer festival nearby sends visitors to {n}
w_festival_season.b: Thousands of people are in town for the weekend and every business on the street feels it.

s_price_spike.b: A shortage upstream pushes the price of your main inputs up. Suppliers quote higher prices for the next weeks.

opts.d: Margin gets thinner for a couple of months.
Margin is partly protected. Some customers balk at the higher prices.

opts.l: Buy ahead from a second source
opts.d: Cash up front; prices stay lower for a while.

s_supplier_strike.t: A strike hits the supplier of {n}
s_supplier_strike.b: Workers at your main supplier have walked out. Deliveries are delayed until a deal is reached.

opts.d: Shelves run thin for a while.

opts.l: Buy from a wholesaler at a premium
opts.d: More expensive, but you keep trading.

s_port_delay.t: Port delays hold up goods for {n}
s_port_delay.b: Containers are stuck at the port and some of your stock is late.

s_recall.t: A batch bought for {n} is recalled
s_recall.b: The maker recalls a product you stock because of a safety issue. You must pull it and refund buyers.

opts.d: Costs money; customers see you act fast.
Cheaper, unless it comes out.

s_bankrupt_supplier.t: A small supplier of {n} goes under
s_bankrupt_supplier.b: A minor supplier has closed overnight. You have to find a new one for a part of your range.

s_energy_spike.b: Gas and electricity prices have risen sharply, and the bill is based on the new rate.

opts.d: Higher bills for a while.

opts.l: Cut hours and switch things off
opts.d: Saves energy, and some sales.

s_fuel_up.b: Diesel and petrol cost noticeably more at the pump.

s_fuel_down.b: Pump prices have eased and the fuel bill falls for a couple of months.

s_commodity_fall.b: A good harvest and falling freight rates bring your main costs down for a while.

s_new_supplier_offer.t: A new supplier offers {n} better terms
s_new_supplier_offer.b: A rival of your supplier wants your business and offers a better price for a trial order.

opts.d: Quality is unknown, but prices are better.

opts.l: Use the offer to haggle with your own supplier
opts.d: Your supplier may match it.

s_bulk_buy.t: Surplus stock is on sale for {n}
s_bulk_buy.b: A wholesaler is clearing out surplus goods at a discount if you take a larger lot.

opts.d: Ties up cash in stock, but cuts your cost for a few weeks.
Nothing changes.

s_late_delivery.b: A supplier misses its slot. Some products are out of stock for a few days.

s_wrong_goods.b: A supplier sent the wrong items. It takes days to get them swapped.

s_damaged_shipment.b: A pallet arrived crushed. The carrier disputes who is responsible.

s_packaging_cost.b: Boxes, bottles and wrapping cost more after a price rise at the maker.

s_machine_part.t: A spare part for {n} is hard to find
s_machine_part.b: A key part is on back order. The machine runs at reduced speed until it arrives.

opts.d: Output stays lower for a few weeks.
Quick and expensive.

s_tariff.b: A government raises duties on goods you import. Your costs go up until you adjust.

opts.d: Margins are squeezed for a quarter.
Protects margin; some customers trade down.

s_local_sourcing.t: A local producer offers to supply {n}
s_local_sourcing.b: A nearby farm or workshop offers fresh goods with shorter delivery times. Customers like the story.

opts.d: Dearer stock, and people may like the local story.
Nothing changes.

s_freight_rates.b: Shipping lines raise their rates after a squeeze on capacity.

s_cold_chain.b: A cold room breaks down overnight and chilled stock warms up.

opts.l: Bin the affected stock and repair now
opts.d: A clean loss, and the fridge is back by evening.
Saves some stock, but it risks a complaint.

d_viral_post.b: A customer's video about {n} is shared by thousands of people. Orders and enquiries come in all week.

d_new_competitor.b: A well-funded newcomer opens nearby with an opening offer. Some customers will try it.

opts.d: Costs margin for a while, and holds more customers.

opts.l: Ignore them and focus on service
opts.d: Some customers leave, but the loyal ones stay.
Keeps your best customers close.

d_competitor_closes.b: A rival nearby has shut its doors. Some of its customers will look for a new place.

d_bad_review_wave.t: A wave of bad reviews for {n}
d_bad_review_wave.b: Several unhappy customers post one-star reviews in the same week.

opts.d: Takes time, and shows you care.
Most people forget. Some do not.

d_five_star.t: A glowing review of {n} is widely read
d_five_star.b: A well-known reviewer or blogger gave {n} five stars. People are mentioning it.

d_local_festival.t: A local festival comes to town near {n}
d_local_festival.b: The town is hosting a three-day festival. Crowds are expected.

opts.d: A cost now, and a good chance of a strong weekend.
You get some of the extra trade anyway.

d_trade_fair.b: A regional trade fair has a stand free. Business buyers walk the halls.

opts.d: The stand and a few days of work. Leads may follow, or not.
Nothing changes.

d_trend_product.t: A trend plays to the strengths of {n}
d_trend_product.b: Magazines and social media are talking about what you do. Searches are up in your area.

d_price_war.b: Competitors start cutting prices. Customers compare offers.

opts.d: You keep the margin and lose some volume.
You keep customers but earn less on each.

d_sales_slump.b: Nothing special went wrong: there are simply fewer customers than usual for a few weeks.

d_busy_spell.b: Enquiries pick up for no obvious reason. The phone keeps ringing.

d_big_order.t: A business customer places a big order with {n}
d_big_order.b: A company wants a one-off order well above your usual size, with payment on invoice.

opts.d: Extra revenue, paid in 45 days, if you can deliver.
Cash up front, and the customer may walk away.

d_customer_complaint.b: A customer is posting about a poor experience and tagging your business.

opts.d: A small cost. They may still post about it.
Others may agree with you, or pile in.

d_press_feature.b: A journalist has written a friendly piece about your business.

d_influencer_ask.t: An influencer asks for a free service from {n}
d_influencer_ask.b: A local influencer will post about you if you offer something free.

opts.d: It costs a little. It may reach thousands of people or nobody.
Nothing changes.

d_online_boycott.t: A false rumour about {n} spreads online
d_online_boycott.b: A post claims something untrue about your business. It is being shared fast.

opts.d: Calm and public. It can also feed the story.
It may blow over, or grow.

d_tourist_wave.b: A cruise ship and two coach tours arrive in town on the same day.

d_road_works.b: The street in front of your door is dug up for weeks. Fewer people pass by.

opts.l: Put up signs and a special offer
opts.d: A small cost to keep people coming.
Regulars may find a way in, or stay away.

d_new_road.t: A new bus stop opens outside {n}
d_new_road.b: A new route brings more people past your door every day.

d_office_move.t: A large employer moves in nearby
d_office_move.b: A company with hundreds of staff has opened offices a few streets from {n}.

d_factory_closes.b: A local employer has shut down. Spending power falls in the area.

d_repeat_customers.b: Repeat business has been strong, and a few regulars send their friends.

d_seasonal_tail.b: The usual enquiries are fewer this month. Customers are delaying decisions.

d_referral_stream.b: Satisfied customers have started to recommend you. The work comes in without advertising.

d_gift_voucher_wave.b: People buy vouchers as presents. Cash arrives now, and the work comes later.

d_cancellations.b: Several customers cancel at short notice in the same week.

d_event_nearby.t: A big match is on near {n}
d_event_nearby.b: A stadium event this weekend brings tens of thousands of visitors to the area.

d_negative_news.t: A news story about your industry hurts trust in {n}
d_negative_news.b: A scandal at another company in your line of business makes customers cautious.

opts.d: A small outlay, and it keeps the story alive a little longer.
Wait for it to pass.

d_member_surge.t: A referral drive pays off at {n}
d_member_surge.b: A friend-brings-a-friend week has brought a surge of new sign-ups.

d_corporate_account.t: A company wants a standing account with {n}
d_corporate_account.b: A local firm wants to use you every month for its staff, at a discount.

opts.l: Offer 10% off for a yearly deal
opts.d: Steady volume at a lower margin. Needs room in the schedule.
No change.

t_flu_wave.t: Flu goes round the team at {n}
t_flu_wave.b: Several people are off sick at the same time.

t_illness_key.t: A key person at {n} is off sick
t_illness_key.b: Your most experienced person is out for a couple of weeks.

opts.d: Costs money and keeps things running.
No cost, but output dips.

t_burnout.t: The team at {n} is running on empty
t_burnout.b: After weeks of long days the team is tired and mistakes are creeping in.

opts.d: Costs a day of output and brings the energy back.
Output holds for now, but people may leave.

t_poached.t: A rival tries to hire your best person at {n}
t_poached.b: A competitor offers your strongest employee a big pay rise.

opts.d: A permanent raise for them, and they will most likely stay.

opts.l: Offer a smaller raise and a bonus
opts.d: Cheaper, and there is a risk they leave anyway.
No cost now. A gap in the team and a hiring job.

t_star_employee.b: One of your people has quietly become the reason customers come back.

opts.d: A one-off cost, and a better mood in the team.
A raise and more responsibility. They may grow into it.

t_good_hire.t: A new hire settles in quickly at {n}
t_good_hire.b: The latest recruit is up to speed faster than expected.

t_union_ask.t: Staff at {n} ask for a raise
t_union_ask.b: Employees say rents and food cost more and ask for a pay increase.

opts.d: A small permanent increase in payroll.
Cheaper, and it does not last.
Some may leave, and the mood suffers.

t_resignation.b: An experienced team member hands in notice after finding a job elsewhere.

t_late_arrivals.b: Several people have started arriving late and customers wait.

t_training_offer.t: A training day is offered to the team at {n}
t_training_offer.b: A local provider offers a subsidised course on skills that matter for your work.

opts.d: A cost and a day of lost output. Whether it sticks depends on the team.
Nothing changes.

t_injury.t: An employee is hurt at work at {n}
t_injury.b: An accident has left one employee off work for several weeks.

opts.d: The right thing to do. Insurance helps if you have it.
Cheaper now, but you risk a claim and bad blood.

t_pregnancy_leave.t: An employee at {n} goes on parental leave
t_pregnancy_leave.b: A valued employee is leaving for several months on parental leave.

t_team_event.t: The team at {n} suggests a day out
t_team_event.b: Staff suggest a day out together. It costs a little and lifts the mood.

opts.d: A small cost. A good night out lifts the team, a flat one does not.
Nothing changes.

t_hiring_wave.b: Unemployment is low. Applicants are few, and those who apply want more money.

t_conflict.t: Two people at {n} are not speaking
t_conflict.b: A dispute between two employees is disturbing the team.

opts.l: Sit them down and sort it out
opts.d: A few hours of your time. It can clear the air or sharpen it.
It might.

t_overtime_peak.b: Work is piling up, and the team can handle it with overtime.

opts.d: The work gets done, at a premium.
Some work waits.

t_apprentice.t: A school offers an apprentice to {n}
t_apprentice.b: A local college has a motivated apprentice looking for a placement.

opts.d: Teaching time and a small wage. They may turn out well.
Nothing changes.

t_pay_gap_found.b: Two employees discovered they are paid differently for the same work. Others want to know too.

opts.d: A permanent increase for some people.
Fair if the reasons are good. The mood suffers.

t_holiday_cover.b: Too many people want the same weeks off.

opts.d: Costs money, and keeps things going.
Saves money. How the team takes it depends on the mood.

t_stealing_staff.b: Takings do not match the till. Someone on the team may have been dipping in.

opts.d: A little cost. Likely to find what happened and stop it.
No cost to find out, and it may happen again.

t_great_week.t: The team at {n} has a great week
t_great_week.b: Everything clicks. Customers are happy and the team is proud.

t_remote_request.t: Staff at {n} ask to work from home two days a week
t_remote_request.b: Several people in office roles would like to work from home part of the week.

opts.d: Happier people, a little less control.
Some people grumble.

r_inspection_ok.t: An inspection finds nothing wrong at {n}
r_inspection_ok.b: An inspector visits and signs off with no remarks. Your records are in order.

r_inspection_notice.t: An inspector leaves a notice at {n}
r_inspection_notice.b: Minor issues are found during a routine visit. They must be fixed within weeks.

opts.d: A small outlay and a clean record.
Cheaper now, with a fine if it is checked again.

r_new_tax_rule.b: The government changes a rule on reporting and accounts. Your accountant needs extra hours to adapt.

r_tax_audit_clean.t: The tax office checks the books of {n}
r_tax_audit_clean.b: An auditor reviews last year's return. Your accounts are in good order, but it takes time.

r_permit_renewal.t: A permit at {n} is up for renewal
r_permit_renewal.b: A licence is expiring. The renewal fee is due and the council wants to check some details.

r_minimum_wage.b: A higher minimum wage applies from next month. Low-paid roles at {n} are affected.

r_fire_safety.b: The fire service finds the extinguishers are out of date and an exit sign is missing.

opts.d: A small cost.
Cheaper if they do not come back.

r_food_hygiene.b: An inspector checks the kitchen, the fridges and the records.

opts.l: Pass it with a deep clean beforehand
opts.d: Costs a day of cleaning before the visit.
Risk of a poor score and a fine.

r_data_rule.b: New rules on customer data require updates to your forms and systems.

r_noise_complaint.b: The council has received complaints and wants you to lower the volume at night.

opts.d: A cost, and fewer late customers.
Risk of a fine and a licence review.

r_licence_review.b: The authority is reviewing your trading licence after complaints.

opts.l: Hire a lawyer and prepare a defence
opts.d: A cost, and a good chance of a clean outcome.
Cheaper, and riskier.

r_environment_rule.b: Tighter rules on waste and emissions apply from next quarter.

opts.d: Costs now; the rule may still change.
Cheaper for now, with a risk of a fine.

r_consumer_complaint.t: The consumer body asks about a complaint at {n}
r_consumer_complaint.b: A customer complained to the authority. You have to reply with evidence.

opts.l: Reply in full and offer a refund
opts.d: A small cost and a closed case.
May win, may lose.

r_vat_change.t: A VAT or sales tax change hits {n}
r_vat_change.b: The rate on part of your sales changes next month. Prices and invoices need updating.

r_subsidy.b: The region has opened a grant for small firms investing in equipment or training.

opts.d: A day or two on the application. Not every application succeeds.
Nothing changes.

r_tax_refund.b: An overpayment of tax is corrected and the money comes back.

r_planning_issue.t: The council questions a sign at {n}
r_planning_issue.b: A sign or an extension was built without full planning consent.

opts.d: A fee and a short delay. Consent is not certain.
Free, and you lose the visibility.

r_wasterules.b: Stricter waste sorting means new bins and a higher collection fee.

r_safety_recall_law.t: A product safety rule changes at {n}
r_safety_recall_law.b: A new standard applies to products like yours. Some stock may not be sold any more.

opts.l: Pull the old stock and replace it
opts.d: A clean break, and a cost.

opts.l: Sell it until it is checked
opts.d: Risk of a fine if inspected.

r_trading_hours.t: The council changes trading hours around {n}
r_trading_hours.b: New rules allow longer opening hours in your street. Competitors may follow.

r_drivers_hours.t: A roadside check stops one of your vehicles
r_drivers_hours.b: Inspectors check drivers' hours and the vehicle's condition.

opts.l: Pay the small fine and fix it
opts.d: Quick and clean.
May cancel the fine, or raise it.

f_rate_up.b: The central bank raises rates. Variable-rate loans cost more every month.

opts.d: Costs a little more each month for a while.
Cash now, a smaller interest bill later.

f_rate_down.b: Lower rates make borrowing cheaper and customers a little more confident.

f_late_payer.t: A customer of {n} is paying late
f_late_payer.b: A business customer is a month behind on an invoice and not answering calls.

opts.d: Most customers pay within a couple of weeks.

opts.l: Offer a discount for quick payment
opts.d: You get the cash, but lose a slice of it.
Free, but they may never pay.

f_bad_debt.b: A customer who owes you money has gone into insolvency. You may get nothing.

opts.d: A fee. You may get part of it back.
No effort, no hope.

f_fraud_attempt.b: An email posing as a supplier asks you to change bank details on an invoice.

opts.d: A delay. If the request is real, the supplier charges a late fee.
Paid on time. If it is fraud, the money is gone.

f_card_fraud.b: Several card payments were disputed by customers. The bank takes the money back.

f_bank_fee_rise.t: The bank raises its fees on {n}
f_bank_fee_rise.b: Account and card fees are up from next month.

f_loan_offer.t: A bank pre-approves a loan for {n}
f_loan_offer.b: The bank has offered a small credit line at a fair rate. Debt can help you grow, and it can also hurt.

opts.d: Nothing changes.
Cash now, interest later. Be careful.

f_cash_squeeze.t: A tight month for cash at {n}
f_cash_squeeze.b: Invoices are due before your customers pay. Cash is thin for a few weeks.

f_overpaid_supplier.b: A supplier found it had overcharged you and refunds the difference.

f_invoice_error.b: A mistake in billing meant a customer was not charged. It is too late to recover.

f_insurance_premium.b: Your insurer raises premiums after a rough year for its industry.

f_early_payment.b: A large customer settles an invoice weeks ahead of the due date.

f_currency_swing_up.t: A weaker currency raises costs for {n}
f_currency_swing_up.b: Your currency has dropped against the dollar and the euro. Imported goods are more expensive.

f_currency_swing_down.t: A stronger currency cuts costs for {n}
f_currency_swing_down.b: Your currency is up against others. Imported goods are cheaper for a while.

f_tax_surprise.t: An extra tax bill arrives at {n}
f_tax_surprise.b: A corrected assessment adds to the amount due for last year.

f_credit_note.t: A pleasant surprise in the bank account of {n}
f_credit_note.b: A forgotten deposit is returned by a supplier.

f_equipment_finance.t: A leasing company pitches equipment finance to {n}
f_equipment_finance.b: A leasing firm offers to spread the cost of new equipment over four years.

opts.d: More capacity, with a payment every month for a year.
Nothing changes.

f_payment_terms.t: A big customer asks for longer payment terms
f_payment_terms.b: A large buyer wants 60 days instead of 30. They say other suppliers agreed.

opts.d: Keeps the work, ties up cash.
Protects your cash and may lose some work.

f_check_account.b: A review of your books finds a missed allowance.

f_loan_review.t: The bank reviews the loan of {n}
f_loan_review.b: A routine review asks for updated accounts and a fee.

m_recession.b: The economy has slowed and households and firms are cutting spending. Customers of {n} are more careful.

opts.d: Protects the margin and keeps prices steady.

opts.l: Cut prices to hold on to customers
opts.d: Keeps volume up, margin down.

m_boom.b: Wages are rising and customers are in a good mood. Business is picking up for {n}.

m_inflation_spike.b: Inflation surprises on the upside. Everything {n} buys costs more.

opts.d: Protects margin, and customers grumble.
Keeps customers, costs margin.

m_consumer_confidence.b: Surveys show households feel better about their money. Spending on small treats rises.

m_consumer_gloom.b: A gloomy survey and rising bills make households pull back from non-essentials.

m_energy_crisis.b: Gas and electricity prices have jumped across the region. Every business feels it in its bills.

opts.d: Higher bills for months.
Saves money and customers.

m_strong_currency.b: A stronger currency makes imports cheaper and exports harder to sell.

m_weak_currency.b: A weaker currency makes imports dearer and local goods more attractive.

m_tourism_boom.b: Visitor numbers are up and hotels are full. Businesses in your area feel it.

m_housing_slump.b: Fewer homes are sold and built. Related trades feel it.

m_housing_boom.b: Sales and building activity are rising. Related trades are busy.

m_rate_shock.b: Higher mortgage payments leave less to spend on eating out and gifts.

m_wage_growth.b: Households have more money to spend. Retailers and venues benefit.

m_trade_war.b: Duties between big economies disrupt supply chains and exports.

opts.d: A few months of thinner margin.
Costs money and takes time.

m_freight_boom.b: Businesses are moving more goods and capacity is tight. Carriers can raise their prices.

m_labour_shortage.t: A labour shortage hits the region
m_labour_shortage.b: Many employers cannot find people. Wages are going up everywhere.

m_cheap_credit.b: Banks are lending freely, and customers finance more purchases.

m_energy_cheap.b: A mild winter and plentiful supply bring energy bills down.

m_crypto_wave.t: A market boom lifts luxury spending
m_crypto_wave.b: People who made money on markets spend it in restaurants and hotels.

m_stock_crash.b: A stock market drop makes wealthy customers cautious about spending.

p_friend_invites.t: A friend invites you to a weekend away
p_friend_invites.b: An old friend has booked a cabin and wants you to come. It would mean a long weekend off.

opts.d: You come back refreshed, and the business runs itself for a few days.
The business gets your full attention.

p_media_interest.t: A podcast wants to interview you about {n}
p_media_interest.b: A local business podcast would like you as a guest.

opts.d: A few hours of your time. It can go either way.
Nothing changes.

p_charity_ask.t: A local charity asks {n} for a donation
p_charity_ask.b: A children's charity is raising money and asks local businesses to help.

opts.d: A little money. People may notice, or not.
Nothing changes.

p_school_visit.t: A school asks {n} to host a visit
p_school_visit.b: A class would like to see how your business works.

p_business_breakfast.t: The chamber of commerce invites you to breakfast
p_business_breakfast.b: Local business owners meet once a month. Good contacts come from these.

opts.d: A morning out of the business. Good leads come now and then.
Nothing changes.

p_neighbour_tip.t: A neighbour tips you off about {n}
p_neighbour_tip.b: A neighbour tells you a big employer is looking for suppliers like you.

opts.d: A few calls and a visit. May lead to nothing.
Nothing changes.

p_award_nomination.t: {n} is nominated for a local award
p_award_nomination.b: Customers have nominated your business in the local awards.

p_university.t: A university asks {n} to take on a project
p_university.b: A university group wants a real company to work with. Students bring fresh ideas.

opts.d: Time from you and the team. Students may bring ideas.
Nothing changes.

p_relative_wedding.t: A family wedding takes you away from {n}
p_relative_wedding.b: A close relative's wedding takes several days of your time.

opts.d: Costs money, and keeps things going.

opts.l: Close for a day or two
opts.d: Costs a day or two of sales.

p_mentor.t: A retired owner offers to mentor you
p_mentor.b: A well-known local business owner, now retired, has offered to meet you once a month.

opts.d: Hours away from the business each week. It may improve how you run things.
Nothing changes.

p_old_friend_customer.t: An old friend sends business to {n}
p_old_friend_customer.b: A friend you worked with years ago now runs a company and wants to use you.

p_team_dinner.t: A supplier invites you to dinner
p_team_dinner.b: A key supplier wants to meet you in person and talk about next year.

opts.d: An evening out. You may get better prices.
Nothing changes.

p_local_newspaper.t: The local paper offers {n} an advertising deal
p_local_newspaper.b: A salesperson at the newspaper offers a package of adverts at a discount.

opts.d: Local reach, but fewer people read papers than before.
Nothing changes.

p_hometown_pride.t: The mayor praises {n} in a speech
p_hometown_pride.b: A local politician mentions your business as an example in a speech.

p_scam_call.t: A caller says your power will be cut today
p_scam_call.b: Someone claiming to be from your energy company says a bill is overdue and asks for payment by phone.

opts.l: Hang up and call the company back
opts.d: Takes time. If the bill was real, a late fee follows.
The power stays on, if the caller was real.

p_burglary_attempt.b: Thieves tried to get in overnight. The door is damaged and nothing was taken.

p_theft_stock.b: A group of thieves clears part of a shelf while staff are busy.

p_vandalism.b: Graffiti and broken windows greet you in the morning.

p_cyber_phishing.t: A phishing email fools someone at {n}
p_cyber_phishing.b: An employee clicks a bad link and a criminal gets into your mailbox.

opts.l: Change passwords, call the IT help and tell customers
opts.d: Some cost and a few awkward calls.
It may be fine, or it may not.

p_ransomware.b: Criminals demand money to unlock your files. Customers cannot book or pay.

opts.d: Slow and costly.
May get the files back. Or not.

p_fire_small.b: A small fire in the back rooms causes smoke and water damage. You have to close for a few days.

opts.d: Closed for a short time. Costly if uninsured.

opts.l: Do the minimum and reopen quickly
opts.d: Cheaper, with lingering damage.

p_neighbour_dispute.t: A dispute with the neighbour over {n}
p_neighbour_dispute.b: A neighbour claims your bins and deliveries block the shared yard.

opts.d: Quick, and it costs you.
May cost lawyers and goodwill, or nothing.

p_celebrity_visit.b: A well-known face has dropped in. Photos are on social media within the hour.

p_sports_win.t: The local team wins the cup
p_sports_win.b: The whole town is celebrating, and the party spills into your area.

p_power_cut.b: The grid fails in your area for part of a day.

p_water_main.b: Water is cut for a day while the main is repaired.

p_internet_down.b: Your connection fails for a day. Card payments and bookings are affected.

p_covid_style.t: A health scare sends customers home
p_covid_style.b: Reports of an outbreak make people avoid crowded places for a few weeks. Trade at {n} falls sharply.

opts.l: Shift to delivery and takeaway where you can
opts.d: Costs money to set up. Holds on to part of your income.
No cost. It may pass quickly, or not.

k_no_oil_down.t: Oil prices fall and the local economy cools
k_no_oil_down.b: Lower oil prices slow investment in the north sea and the services around it.

k_no_midnight_sun.b: Long bright evenings keep people out and spending.

k_uk_bank_holiday.b: A long weekend brings day trippers and families.

k_us_thanksgiving.b: Holiday shoppers and travellers fill the streets.

k_de_energy.b: Industrial users face higher power costs than their neighbours.

k_jp_typhoon.b: Transport stops for a day and shops close early.

k_au_bushfire_smoke.b: Smoke keeps people indoors and outdoor trade down.

k_es_siesta_summer.b: Opening hours shift later and tourists fill the evenings.

k_lt_euro_funds.b: A regional development programme has opened a call for small business investment.

opts.d: Some effort on the application. Not every one succeeds.
Nothing changes.

k_ch_franc.t: A strong currency makes exports harder to sell
k_ch_franc.b: Local goods cost more abroad and visitors find prices high.

k_ae_expo.t: A large exhibition fills the hotels
k_ae_expo.b: Visitors arrive in large numbers and hotels, taxis and restaurants are busy.

k_ca_cold.b: A deep freeze slows traffic and keeps people home.

k_nl_bike_rain.b: People cycle less in the rain and take shelter in cafes.
